title: Mouse highlighter draws a circle on desktop upon activation.
summary: Mouse Highlighter in preview v0.101.2572 reportedly shows the intended ripple effect when activated but also leaves a blue circle stuck on the desktop until reboot.

status.label: Current-build reproduction ready
status.detail: The report is on the current preview build and includes a bug report ZIP; maintainers should reproduce the activation path and inspect whether Mouse Highlighter leaves an always-on or button-state visual alive.

next_action.label: Reproduce Mouse Highlighter stuck circle
next_action.reason: The symptom is specific enough for a maintainer-side reproduction pass, and code inspection leaves multiple plausible visual-state paths.

judgment.rationale: The reporter supplied a current preview version, a direct activation scenario, and a PowerToys bug report ZIP. The lightweight code inspection found that Mouse Highlighter creates an initial always/idle visual on activation and separate ripple/button visuals with timers and fade animations, so a controlled repro trace is needed to determine which visual remains visible and why it is not cleared.
evidence: The issue targets PowerToys 0.101.2572 Preview and the Mouse Utilities area.
The reported reproduction is to activate Mouse Highlighter with the activation shortcut.
Actual behavior says the feature activates with the expected ripple effect and also draws a blue circle on the desktop that cannot be removed without rebooting.
MouseHighlighter::StartDrawing creates an initial MouseButton::None drawing point when activation starts.
MouseHighlighter handles ripple mode with hold timers, button state, fade animations, and ClearDrawing/StopDrawing paths that can distinguish stale always-on visuals from stale click/hold visuals.
judgment.recommended_action: Run a controlled maintainer reproduction using the attached diagnostics and current Mouse Highlighter settings, then inspect whether activation leaves m_alwaysPointer, a ripple hold shape, or overlay state visible after the effect should fade.

fix_assessment.rationale: A PowerToys code fix is likely applicable if reproduced, but the lightweight pass cannot yet distinguish whether the stuck blue circle is the activation-created always pointer, a right-button/ripple hold visual, a stale composition shape, or a settings-specific overlay state.

issue_context.summary: Activating Mouse Highlighter on the preview build reportedly produces the expected ripple effect plus an extra blue desktop circle that persists until reboot.
known_information: Installation methods selected: GitHub and PowerToys auto-update.
The reporter attached a PowerToys bug report ZIP.
There are no public comments or existing upstream author-feedback requests.
inferences: Because the normal ripple appears, the activation shortcut and module startup path are likely running.
The persistent blue circle may be a stale Mouse Highlighter composition visual rather than a failure to start the feature.
The color may correspond to right-button highlighting or a customized always-on/highlight color, but the public report does not identify the exact Mouse Highlighter settings.
issue_context.analysis: The public issue already contains enough current-build evidence for maintainer reproduction. Source inspection shows separate activation, always-pointer, ripple hold, fade, reset, and stop paths; the next useful action is a trace that identifies which object remains visible and whether StopDrawing/ClearDrawing/fade timers execute.
initial_investigation: Reviewed the issue body, labels, comments, updatedAt, and attachment metadata through 2026-09-17T12:23:55Z.
Inspected src/modules/MouseUtils/MouseHighlighter/MouseHighlighter.cpp StartDrawing, AddDrawingPoint, ClearDrawingPoint, ClearDrawing, StopDrawing, HandleMouseEvent, and ripple timer paths.
Inspected src/modules/MouseUtils/MouseHighlighter/MouseHighlighter.h for default colors and ripple defaults.
Inspected src/modules/MouseUtils/MouseHighlighter/dllmain.cpp settings parsing for spotlight and ripple configuration.

reproduce.version_requirement: PowerToys 0.101.2572 Preview or a current build containing the same Mouse Highlighter ripple implementation
prerequisites: Use the reporter's Mouse Highlighter settings from the attached PowerToys bug report ZIP when available
Capture Mouse Highlighter trace/log output around activation and deactivation
steps: Enable Mouse Highlighter and set activation to the same shortcut/settings shown in the attached diagnostic package.
Activate Mouse Highlighter with the activation shortcut.
Observe whether the expected ripple effect appears.
After the ripple fade duration, inspect whether a blue circle remains on the desktop.
If it remains, toggle Mouse Highlighter off and on, then use the activation shortcut again to determine whether StopDrawing or ClearDrawing clears the visual.
Repeat with ripple mode disabled and with the always-on/highlight color alpha set to transparent versus visible to isolate the visual source.
reproduce.expected_result: Mouse Highlighter should show only the configured transient or always-on effect and should clear transient ripple/button visuals after their fade without leaving an unremovable desktop circle.
setup_requirements: Record the active Mouse Highlighter settings: ripple mode, spotlight mode, left/right/highlight colors, opacity, radius, fade delay, fade duration, ripple size, and release-pulse settings.
Capture whether MouseHighlighter::StartDrawing creates an initial MouseButton::None visual with non-zero alpha.
Capture whether the remaining circle corresponds to m_alwaysPointer, m_leftPointer/m_rightPointer, m_leftRippleGlow/m_rightRippleGlow, or spotlight overlay state.
Capture whether StopDrawing, ResetPendingMouseInput, ClearDrawing, and any active hold/fade timers run before the circle remains visible.

upstream_safety.detail: No comments, labels, assignments, closures, or other public mutations were made to microsoft/PowerToys.
